metas.name: Argentina - Catamarca red mountains
metas.note: On the 60, east of Fiambalá, bright red mountains line the road, sometimes quite dramatically. A few of the red hills are embedded in between gray hills in a way that almost looks like a badly colored black and white photograph. Good luck telling it apart from similar roads in Salta and La Rioja! The best method may be the clouds: This road has no clouds, while the one in La Rioja has some low hazy ones to the South (except when it doesn't) and the one in Salta has higher, better defined clouds. It's tough.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - La Rioja red mountains
metas.note: In La Rioja, just north of Talampaya National Park, there is a part of the RN40 with almost blindingly bright red mountains. Good luck telling it apart from similar roads in Catamarca and Salta! The best method may be the clouds: This road has low clouds toward the South (except when it doesn't), while the one in Catamarca is always cloudless and the one in Salta has higher, better defined clouds. It's tough.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - Neuqén sunrise
metas.note: In the North of Neuquén, the Google driver started their day early and the camera did not like it. As the day progresses, the car goes further north and the glitchy colors fade, until only a bit of color noise remains, and finally, around the province border, it starts to look like normal footage.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - Salta red mountains
metas.note: On the 68 in Salta, between Alemania and Cafayate, there's a stretch of red mountains. Compared to the red mountains in La Rioja and Catamarca, the surrounding range is more massive and the red not quite as cartoonish. You may also be able to tell the difference by the clouds: The ones here are high above and relatively defined; the ones in La Rioja, when they appear, are low in the southern sky and kind of hazy, and the coverage in Catamarca is cloudless.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - Tucuman mist road
metas.note: On the 65 in Tucuman, leading west to the Catamarca border near Parque Nacional Aconquija, the Google car drove through what appears to be mist thick enough to clog your windpipe.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Bolivia - Death road
metas.note: Northeast of La Paz, there is an unpaved road that is cloudy and wet and narrow and looks like a nightmare to drive. Yet, apparently, it is frequented by mountain bikers a whole lot.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Amapá blur
metas.note: Gen 4 coverage in the state of Amapá has a distinct blur in the front right of the panorama. Make sure you have the striped car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Brown mushroom insulator
metas.note: Brown mushroom insulators appear in (mostly urban) Pernambuco.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - East of Belo QR Code
metas.note: A small region just east of Belo Horizonte has a little QR code sticker on almost every pole that's found nowhere else in the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Lollipop insulator
metas.note: In the states of Rio Grande do Norte, Paraíba and Pernambuco, these two types of insulators on thin stems can be found. One looks like a thick cone that gets thinner toward the bottom, and the other has a sort of rounded silhouette - careful, it's easy to confuse with another insulator that can also be found elsewhere, with three equal width ridges. The bottom ridge has to be substantially smaller in order to create the round shape.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Maranhao black and white pickup
metas.note: In northern Maranhao, Google used a recognizable pickup truck with a white cab and a black bed for some footage around Lencois Maranhenses National Park
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Paraná black dot
metas.note: If you see a little square black dot low on the flat side of a ladder pole, you're going to be in Paraná. Other states may have unpainted square indents, some white or silver dots/stickers, but only in Paraná is it ever black. Its absence does not mean you are not in Paraná, and it appears to be a relatively new practice (found mostly on newer poles).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - UFO Trident
metas.note: In rural Maranhao, you will often see trident poles with large, UFO-like insulators. These insulators are common elsewhere as well, but with the trident config it's going to be Maranhao.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - White mushroom insulator
metas.note: The white mushroom insulators are typical for Bahia, but I also found some on the southern border of Pernambuco. They are generally more common in urban areas than in rural ones.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Saskatchewan white bits
metas.note: Yellow center lines in Saskatchewan frequently have tiny white bits in and around them. You can also rarely find them in BC and Yukon, but the landscape there should be different enough to not get them confused.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Chile - Arica/Iquique stick
metas.note: In Arica and Iquique, in the very North of Chile, sometimes there'll be a little stick with a few leaves stuck on the car's back.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/chile for more clues.

metas.name: Colombia - Isla de Providencia car
metas.note: On the tiny Isla de Providencia, Google used a small silver truck with a long antenna
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Colombia - Max north Colombia vibes
metas.note: The northern tip of Colombia looks a lot like Tumbes and Piura in Peru, but with more cacti and a different car
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Colombia - San Andrés car
metas.note: On the small island of San Andrés, Google used a small white truck with no antenna
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Atahualpa road
metas.note: One road on the southern east coast of Ecuador looks a lot like a gray, dirty, depressing version of Tumbes or Piura, just with more garbage. It has an offshoot with a pretty beach.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Guatemala - Green poles
metas.note: All-green painted metal poles can be found in only a few areas of Guatemala, mostly in the Southeast of the country. They have codes on them that will tell you even more precisely where you are.
metas.footer: Image from Plonkit.net/guatemala

metas.name: India - Bihar 4 red & white stripes
metas.note: If you see red-white-red-white stripes on trees (and rarely poles) that line the road, you will be in Bihar (other regions have similar markings with just three stripes). The paint is often faded considerably.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Bihar 4 yellow & black stripes
metas.note: 4 Yellow-black-yellow-black stripes on poles will usually place you in Bihar. Also appears in Delhi sometimes, but it's much more commonly 5 or more stripes there. 5 and 3 stripes can also rarely be found in Bihar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Delhi 5+ yellow-black stripes
metas.note: 5 or more black&yellow stripes on poles are usually only a Delhi thing. Rarely appears in other places, like Bihar. Sometimes, you will find fewer than 5 stripes on poles in Delhi.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Kerala pole markings
metas.note: Many Kerala poles have a particular yellow marking, usually round, with hand-written Latin script in black.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Mint green electricity counters
metas.note: Mint green to grayish-green electricity counters of this particular design are found in Punjab and Haryana.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Tamil Nadu stripes
metas.note: Poles and trees in Tamil Nadu have a particular white-black-white marking.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Bali black cab
metas.note: A car with a big black cab and an open back in which a variety of people ride is found in eastern Bali, south of Mount Agung
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Bali vampire hunter car
metas.note: A car with black railings and (usually) a big wooden stake lying in the bed can be found in eastern Bali, south of Mount Agung
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Aomori diamond
metas.note:
Aomori road paint diamonds:

  • Full size
  • Two L shapes overlapping clockwise on the wide angles
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Kagawa diamond
metas.note:
Kagawa road paint diamonds:

  • Full size
  • Kung Fu salutation pattern
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Nara & Wakayama diamond
metas.note:
Nara and Wakayama road paint diamonds:

  • Full size
  • Four elements arranged to overlap clockwise
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Nara small diamond
metas.note:
(Mostly northern) Nara road paint diamonds:

  • Snack size
  • Four elements arranged to overlap clockwise
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Saga small diamond
metas.note:
Saga road paint diamonds:

  • Snack size & skinny
  • Diamond broken in the middle
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Shizuoka diamond
metas.note:
Shizuoka road paint diamonds:

  • Skinny
  • Kung Fu salutation pattern
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Yamanashi & Nagano diamond
metas.note:
Yamanashi and Nagano road paint diamonds:

  • Skinny
  • Four elements arranged to overlap counter-clockwise
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - Bird poop
metas.note: Only on a very tiny bit of coverage on the C104 in southern Kenya, embedded in Tsavo National Park, the Google car is adorned with two recognizable splats of bird poop. Cheers.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Gunung Mulu car
metas.note: A tiny bit of footage near Gunung Mulu National Park, south of Brunei, was shot with a long silver truck with a chrome rollcage and three logos on the hood
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Jalisco Taiwan/Kansai pole paint
metas.note: In the state of Jalisco, it is common to see poles painted Taiwan style with a black and yellow barberpole pattern, or Kansai style with long vertical black and yellow stripes. Careful: these can very rarely appear in other states
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Altai car
metas.note: North and south of Altai, the Google car in Gen 4 has its tent tied down with four neatly packed straps. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Black object
metas.note: On a short stretch of the road leading to Ulaangrom in the Northwest of the country, east of Tarialan, there is a black object visible on the left side of the truck bed. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Four straps open tent
metas.note: The zipper of tent on the Google car is open on a stretch of road between Tosontsengel and the Teel area. When there are four straps visible, you will be on the eastern part of that coverage. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Into the night
metas.note: On a road in northeastern Mongolia, the Google car drove through sunset into nighttime. There is a second road in the southeast with sunset coverage, which can be distinguished by the driving angle: this one goes east, the one in the South goes north.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Into the night, part 2
metas.note: In southeastern Mongolia, the Google car drove until after sunset. You can see the shadows becoming longer and the footage eventually turns very dark. This can be told apart from the other sunset road in the northeast by the driving angle - this one goes north, the other one goes east.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Messy straps no loop
metas.note: From Bayankhongor to Arvaikheer, Gen 4 coverage will have two straps with a messy knot. The mess is one clump with no loose loops. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Messy straps with loop
metas.note: From Arvaikheer to Ulaanbaatar, Gen 4 coverage will have two straps with a messy knot that has a loose loop. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Messy straps zipper corner
metas.note: Between Altai and Bayankhongor, Gen 4 coverage will have two straps with a messy knot. While further east, the zipper tag is a bit more central, on this part of the road it is all the way left. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Open tent merged straps
metas.note: The zipper of tent on the Google car is open on a stretch of road between Tosontsengel and the Teel area. When there are four straps converging into a single point on the left side, you will be on a north-south bit in the middle of that coverage. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Open tent two straps
metas.note: The zipper of tent on the Google car is open on a stretch of road between Tosontsengel and the Teel area. When there are just two straps visible, you will be on the westernmost part of that coverage. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Perfectly packed
metas.note: West of Altai until about Sharga, the Google car in Gen 4 has its tent tied down with two neatly packed straps, no knots. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Single knot right (2 straps)
metas.note: In the West and Northwest of the country, the tent on the car in Gen4 coverage is usually tied with two straps and a single knot visible in the center of the tent or to the left. When the knot is slightly on the right of the tent, you will be on one specific road between Durvuljin and Uliastai. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Two knots left (2 straps)
metas.note: In the Southwest of the country, the tent on the car in Gen4 coverage is usually tied with two straps and two knots on the right side. If the knots are on the left instead, you will be on one of two specific stretches of road around the Tarvagatai Mountains. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Two knots right (4 straps)
metas.note: Between Khotont and Lun, you will find four straps tying down the tent on the Google car in Gen4, with both knots on the right side. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Two knots, one center (4 straps)
metas.note: Around Tsetserleg, you will find four straps tying down the tent on the Google car in Gen4, with one of the two knots in the center of the tent and the other one on the right side. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Water bottle
metas.note: Between Khyargas Lake and Songino, a water bottle will be visible on the left side of the truck bed. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - 7 digit pole code
metas.note: Black vertical pole markings with 7 digits that start with 1 or 4 (or rarely 3) are found only in western central North Island.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - Auckland and Northland pole code
metas.note: If you see a black vertical pole code with six or seven digits, with or without an extra tag, that starts with a 9, you are going to be in Auckland or further north.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - Christchurch pole code
metas.note: Between the two rivers around Christchurch, you can find 5-character pole codes that start with two letters. They are a little smaller than the vertical black codes in other parts of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - Northern tip pole code
metas.note: Only on the northernmost tip of Northland will you find six-digit-plus-tag pole codes that start with a 2
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - P pole code
metas.note: An area in southeastern Manawatu has pole codes with a P followed by 5 digits
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - Red White Blue Dots
metas.note: On the northeast tip of Northland, you will find little pole stickers in red, white and blue (although not always all three). They can be round or rectangular.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - Warning sticker
metas.note: There are just three areas on North Island with these specific warning stickers on electricity poles
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - White pole code
metas.note: A 6-digits-plus-tag pole code starting with 30 or 31 with inverted colors (black on white) means you are in Auckland or Northland
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Benin City follow cars
metas.note: Benin City has these two unique follow cars: a black and a wine red Toyota SUV without police markings.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: North Macedonia - Smudges
metas.note: In southern and eastern North Macedonia, some roads have recognizable smudges on the camera: A large dead insect on the R1205, a vertical pattern of about four smudges on the PS27, a central smudge (plus more further south) on the easternmost part of the A3, a brown smudge on the lower left center in the southeast of the country, and on the A1 to Bitola, a single smudge higher up to the left with a short section of two brown smudges center left halfway between Bitola and Prilep
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/north-macedonia for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Arequipa vertical sticker
metas.note: A vertical white sticker with blue or red numbers places you in Arequipa Province
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Cloudless 30C
metas.note: The 18C and 5N road in central Peru, south and east from Pucalipa, and the 30C in eastern Peru, curving up to the Bolivian border, are pretty much the only places in the country with a flat profile (no visible mountains), a well-built road, and lush, jungly vegetation with a slightly yellow tint. You can tell which of the two you're on from the clouds: there aren't really any on the 30C, and the 18C/5N will always have substantial clouds.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Cloudy 18C/5N
metas.note: The 18C and 5N road in central Peru, south and east from Pucalipa, and the 30C in eastern Peru, curving up to the Bolivian border, are pretty much the only places in the country with a flat profile (no visible mountains), a well-built road, and lush, jungly vegetation with a slightly yellow tint. You can tell which of the two you're on from the clouds: there aren't really any on the 30C, and the 18C/5N will always have substantial clouds.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Cusco sideways pole numbers
metas.note: In the wider Cusco area and up to the tri-point with Brazil and Bolivia, concrete poles will sometimes have yellow stickers with black numbers going sideways.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Hell road
metas.note: East of Chimbote, there's a road where sundown and clouds conspired to create footage as if from the depths (or rather heights?) of hell.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Locumba bollards
metas.note: Around the town of Locumba, between Moquegua and Tacna, you get bollards that look like half-buried Moquegua type, interspersed with sections with just loose white rocks for bollards.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Moquegua bollards
metas.note: These round white bollards with orange and black markings at the top are only found around the southern Department of Moquegua
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Moquegua-like bollards
metas.note: Bollards with the same color scheme as the Moquegua ones, but in different prism shapes (triangular, quadrangular) and/or with white and red reflectors appear on the 38A through Tacla and Puno and on the 3S south of Ilave. If they appear in Gen 3 coverage, go Ilo (on the coast)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - South sticker
metas.note: If you see a white sticker with blue text on a pole, you will be in the very south, below Arequipa
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Tumbes Vibes
metas.note: Sandy soil, fairly flat, green or withered bushes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Twin pole stickers
metas.note: Two horizontal yellow stickers with black text can be found on concrete poles in a corridor between Tingo Maria and Ayacucho.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - West Piura vibes
metas.note: Super flat desert (a bit hilly northwest though), sandy, sparse bushes
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Bicol Adidas guardrails
metas.note: In an area including Bicol, Catanduanes and Masbate, you will see guardrails marked with three black stripes. Careful: you can get more or fewer than three in other places as well, but if you see three, it is most likely going to be this area.
metas.footer: Check out sleepfor8hx3's Philippines Guide for more info

metas.name: Philippines - Bohol thick insulator stem
metas.note: The stems on which insulators sit at the top of poles is commonly thick or encased in a plastic tube that makes it appear much thicker than usual on the island of Bohol.
metas.footer: For more info, check out Philippines Poles and Insulators by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Davao Occidental quad pancake insulator
metas.note: If you see a quadruple pancake insulator on a pole top, you're going to be on the one road with coverage in Davao Occidental, along the coast, between approximately Don Marcelino and Bukid.
metas.footer: For more info, check out Philippines Poles and Insulators by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - East Samar double pancake insulator
metas.note: Double pancake insulators are very rare, but most likely to be found along the coast of East Samar, from about the height of the island of Hilabaan all the way down to the southern tip.
metas.footer: For more info, check out Philippines Poles and Insulators by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Ilocos Norte and Biliran quad insulator
metas.note: This cylinder with four distinct ridges is most common in Ilocos Norte, but can also be found in southern Biliran.
metas.footer: For more info, check out Philippines Poles and Insulators by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Manila and Ilocos Norte Star Wars insulator
metas.note: This type of insulator that looks like the buildings on Tatooine is most common in northern Luzon and in and around Manila.
metas.footer: For more info, check out Philippines Poles and Insulators by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Manila sausage insulator
metas.note: This grey insulator with lots of small ridges that looks kind of solid is most common in and around Manila, but can rarely be found elsewhere.
metas.footer: For more info, check out Philippines Poles and Insulators by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Mesh poles
metas.note: Flimsy mesh poles are common in the province of Zamboanga Sibugay. They also, rarely, appear in other provinces, but even then you should be on Mindanao.
metas.footer: For more info, check out Philippines Poles and Insulators by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - North Cebu yellow blocks
metas.note: In northern Cebu, you will find gray concrete guard blocks with their edges or sides painted yellow. These are not the only guard blocks in the area, so don't discount northern Cebu if you see, for example, fully yellow concrete blocks or walls and blocks with diagonal black and yellow stripes.
metas.footer: Check out sleepfor8hx3's Philippines Guide for more info

metas.name: Philippines - North Luzon Chile poles
metas.note: Chile poles can be frequently found in northern Luzon, especially Cagayan, but careful - they can also appear, if less commonly, in northern Negros!
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Northwest Leyte and Biliran extender insulators
metas.note: Three ridges plus a long extender at the top to carry the wire are most commonly found in northwestern Leyte and northwestern Biliran.
metas.footer: For more info, check out Philippines Poles and Insulators by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Palawan trike
metas.note: The trikes on the island of Palawan are recognizable by their single wide front window. Many of them look as if they were cosplaying as cars, with emblems and everything.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Panay & Guimaras yellow backboards
metas.note: On the islands of Panay and Guimaras (the little island next to Iloilo), electricity counters are frequently mounted on yellow backboards. These can be horizontal or vertical, metal or wood.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Quezon blue/red blocks
metas.note: In a small area on the isthmus of Quezon province, you will find alternating red and blue guard blocks.
metas.footer: Check out sleepfor8hx3's Philippines Guide for more info

metas.name: Philippines - South Mindanao car
metas.note: In southern Mindanao, in the very South of the Philippines, there is some footage taken with a silver truck with a visible roof rack. Note that this is leftover, unculled old coverage that runs parallel to gen 4 images of the same locations, so you can still get the same roads with a different car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Southern Quezon acne blocks
metas.note: The southern peninsula of Quezon has these sloped concrete blocks with round spots made from small rocks that kind of look like a skin issue. Blocks in this style with straight edges are common throughout the country, and you can get slanted concrete blocks without the acne in other places as well, but the combination is exclusive to this area.
metas.footer: Check out sleepfor8hx3's Philippines Guide for more info

metas.name: South Africa - Koloti boulders
metas.note: In Limpopo, northeast of Polokwane, there are yellow boulders lying around as if a giant dropped his toys.
